title: EDGE: ZPK.TransferFunction merges distinct poles within 100*eps window, wrong numerators
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #70 fuzz/AULHZC] ZPK.TransferFunction gives wrong numerators when distinct poles fall in its merge window. commonDenomPoles and poleSetDifference (zpk.go:369,399) treat poles within 100*eps*(1+|p|) as equal, so a real pole can match a complex one. sortConjugatePairs (zpk.go:322) then re-adds the conjugate and the numerator degree is too high (polynomial_channel.go:90). Repro 1: NewZPKMIMO(zeros {{nil,nil}}, poles {{{1e-14+1e-14i, 1e-14-1e-14i},{1e-15}}}, gains {{1,1}}, dt 0) -> TransferFunction gives Den=[1 -2e-14 2e-28] and Num[0][1] equal to Den, so tf.Eval(10)[0][1] = 1 but zpk.Eval = 0.1. Repro 2 (unit scale): poles {1+-1e-15i} and {1} -> Den=[1 -2 1], Num1=[1 -2 1], tf(3)[1] = 1 vs zpk(3) = 0.5. MATLAB tf(zpk) converts each channel separately and gets this right. FuzzZPKToTF skips these rows with reason 'distinct row poles within the ZPK pole-merge tolerance'.

title: EDGE: DCGain wrong finite value / wrong Inf next to near-DC or exact DC poles
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The A solve fails (cond 1.4e21) and poleSpacing near=true (pole -1.88e-8). DCGain returns +9.684e11. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Example dc9: a continuous upper-triangular A with diagonal entries -2.89e-5, -3.09e-11, -1.75e-5, ... gives DCGain [-Inf, -78626.6], while FreqResponse(0) and the exact big.Rat solve give [-1.1129e18, -3.0967e18]. Its DCGain is finite but has relative error 5e-5 against the exact value (789372732529716 vs 789410222466333), and FreqResponse(0) is +Inf in every entry. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). The value comes from dcGainByStructuralEntries. dcGainByBlockLaurent declines because it needs a 1x1 block with A_kk == x0, although the branch's exactDetIsZero could detect this block. Files: response.go dcGainByStructuralEntries / dcGainByBlockLaurent.


Fuzz wave 12f reports folded in:

[w12f #31] CORE: DCGain returns a finite value for an exact integrator, so Bandwidth returns +Inf, nil instead of ErrInvalidArgument. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1,A=[-1000 10; 0 0], b=[1;1], c=[1 1], d=0). Exact residue at s=0 is 1.01, so the DC gain is infinite (MATLAB dcgain gives Inf). DCGain returns -3.47e13 and Bandwidth(sys,-3) returns +Inf with nil error, on both arm64 and GOARCH=amd64. A sweep of A=[a k; 0 0], b=c=[1 1], with a in {-1..-1e3, 7, 250, 2.5e4} and k in {10..1e6}: 23/90 wrong on arm64, 18/90 on amd64, some with the wrong sign. [w14 #2] FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 (‖A‖≈4e43) passes only by luck. TF keeps the z=1 integrator only through the ‖c‖-relative test for c being zero. title: CORE: TunePID PD mixed-sign gains on integrating plants (pidTuningDCSign returns 0)
body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Cross-ref FRD wrong-sign task (stable plants, real instability) — this one is stable designs, sign policy only.

[w14 #14 pidtune/SIVH4J] TunePID PD returns gains of opposite sign on integrating plants. Repro: TransferFunc num {8.2}, den {1,-1}, Dt 0.05, then StateSpace and TunePID(ctx, sys, PidtunePD, PIDTuningOptions{}). It returns Kp 0.0344, Kd -0.0019; with PhaseMargin 30 it returns Kp 0.0273, Kd -0.0036. Pidtune PD on the same plant gives same-sign gains (Kp 0.0378, Kd +3.1e-4, Tf 8.2e-4), and MATLAB pidtune never gives mixed signs. IP3XIC k=10 PD does the same (fix: Kp 0.79, Kd -1.23e5). The designs are stable with |S| <= 4, so this is about the sign policy, not robustness. Cause: pidTuningDCSign returns 0 once Pidtune recognises an integrator, so pidTuningSignConsistent accepts any mix of signs (pid_tuning.go, pidTuningDCSign and pidTuningSignConsistent; TunePID default PD path). Owner call: whether integrating plants should require same-sign gains, perhaps using the sign of the integrator's residue. Note SIVH4J's new test pins two such mixed-sign PD designs as acceptable for |S|.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-20): require same-sign gains; the sign comes from the integrator residue
MATLAB pidtune never returns mixed signs, and Pidtune already gives same-sign gains on the same plant.
- When integratingDCGain (internal dcGain(false)) is ±Inf, pidTuningDCSign returns sign(integratingDCGain) instead of 0.
- Do not touch the unstable-plant sign rule (YVAIMU / pidtuneGainSign); reuse it.
- Allowed flips: mixed-sign → same-sign design, or mixed-sign → unattainable. BLOCKING: a same-sign base design that changes and then fails the oracle.
- Re-pin the two mixed-sign PD designs in the SIVH4J test.
Priority CORE. Put it in the wave 15 pidtune track together with GMED3W and EPFTFX.

body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). MATLAB minreal prescales and documents tol=sqrt(eps); current default is no Equalize and ctrbf floor 10*n*||A||_1*eps. Measured trade-offs below.

[w14 #3 tf/PKUP2G 65BPNH] Reduce on badly scaled models without Equalize: in the Kalman sweep at d=4 (state scales 10^±4, KALMAN_SWEEP_DIAG=4 KALMAN_SWEEP_N=4000), 65/4000 reduced realizations have response error >1e-6 (base 171). With Equalize forced on: d=4 response 171 fixed / 1 regressed, order 92 regressed; d=0 order 477 fixed / 15 regressed. Owner decision: default prescaling, as MATLAB minreal prescales. Files: minimal.go Reduce/equalize.

[w14 #9 tf/review1] Owner parity question: Reduce/MinimalRealization use the ctrbf floor (10·n·||A||₁·eps) rather than MATLAB minreal's documented sqrt(eps). On my sweep, 82 Kalman-structured over-counts (most with hidden unstable states kept) resolve with Tol 1.8-3.2x the default, and all resolve below sqrt(eps)-scale tolerances without any under-count. The branch's doc gives the counter-case (weakly coupled slow plants). Files: minimal.go ReduceOpts.Tol, staircase.go ctrbfFloor.

[w14 #5 tf/review] Owner decision, Reduce default Tol (review item 6): MATLAB minreal documents tol = sqrt(eps). Measured with that default: TestReduceIssue26PIPlantLoop drops to order 1; KALMAN_SWEEP_DIAG=3 gives 174 under-counts and 277 response errors (base 9); with Equalize forced there are still O(1) response errors at the correct order (e.g. rr=4.71 on id 1185 and 12.5 on id 1609, seed PCG(id, 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15), kB=8). Kept n²·eps plus the ctrbf floor. Files: minimal.go Reduce, staircase_sweep_test.go.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-20, reconciled with MathWorks doc)
The MathWorks minreal page does not mention balancing, scaling, prescaling or ssbal. Its Algorithms section says only "Transfer functions are first converted to zero-pole-gain form", and the default tol is sqrt(eps), a pole-zero matching tolerance in a different algorithm. Parity is silent on Equalize.
- Tol: keep the ctrbf floor. ReduceOpts.Tol stays as the user override. Document why sqrt(eps) is not copied: it is a different quantity, and the measured sqrt(eps) default gave 174 under-counts and 277 response errors at d=3, and dropped TestReduceIssue26PIPlantLoop to order 1.
- Equalize: decide by data. Evaluate Equalize-on TOGETHER with one shared ctrbf floor across Reduce, CtrbF and ObsvF on the d=0..4 Kalman sweep.

Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. [w14 #36 delayfreq/review] Nyquist returns a finite RHPZerosCL for delayed loops with |D| >= 1, which have infinitely many closed-loop RHP roots. With L(j∞) = D, |D| > 1 and a delay, the closed loop is a neutral system whose roots approach Re s = ln|D|/τ > 0, so no finite count is correct. Branch I/O form returns 578 with no error (base 68). The PullDelaysToLFT form returns ErrDelayUnsupported on the branch and ErrSingularTransform on base. More cases from the same PCG(3,5) sweep: d=1.269, τ=2.713 gives 996; d=1.427, τ=2.950 gives 840; d=1.0144, τ=2.225 gives 5200. Files: nyquist.go (continuousHalf tail when HasDelay && closure != 0; nyquistEncirclements). Suggested: return ErrDelayUnsupported, or another documented error, when |D| >= 1 and the loop is delayed, following MATLAB semantics.

[w14 #41 delayfreq/review2] Optional, low priority. Nyquist on loops with wc*tau above about 1e5 reports ErrSingularTransform ('1+L = 0 on the contour') rather than a count or ErrDelayUnsupported, even within the 2^21 sample budget. Repro: L = 33894/(s+18.92)*e^{-5.23s}, built with NewFromSlices(1,1,1,{-18.92},{1},{33894},{0},0) and SetInputDelay({5.23}); the error comes from Nyquist(nil,0). The branch's count is not wrong, and base returned a count (1242) that is wrong by about 45x against the true value of about 5.6e4. The only issue is the error type; MATLAB's nyquist does not count encirclements. File it only if a clearer error class is wanted (files: nyquist.go refine and the at() on-contour check).

Relative Riccati residual (dareRelResidual) at base 0c02feb and 4a25ae4: about 7e-14 at n=60..64, then 0.32 (n=65), 0.24 (66), 0.15 (67), 0.078 (68), 0.48 (70), 0.022 (100), 0.015 (120). body:

[w14 #35 delayfreq/WYLHSA] Pre-existing, numerically extreme, but it stops FuzzFreqResponse within 1-3 minutes: Nyquist RHPPoles is 1 where the fuzz oracle expects 2, for discrete 2-state loops with eig(A) about {1.0018, 5.5e9}. Files: nyquist.go classifyNyquistBoundary, nyquist_fuzz_test.go fzNyqPoleClass. Either the library or the fuzz harness needs to change; that call is yours.

[w14 #37 delayfreq/review0] [EDGE, pre-existing on 0c02feb] Nyquist reports RHPPoles=1 for a discrete model with two exactly unstable poles. title: CORE: Dgges SortSelected rejects borderline 2x2 swaps (Netlib parity): controlsys needs fallback (Dare/ordered Schur)
body:
From gonum ZHGFWA (gonum PR #35 parity test TestDtgex2NetlibBorderlineAcceptance). The gonum QZ matches Netlib to about 1e-16, but Dtgex2's swap acceptance on borderline 2x2/2x2 blocks is decided by rounding in both libraries: BQRA21 = 5.455e-14 against THRESHA = 5.560e-14 in Netlib, while gonum gets 1.25e-13 and rejects. Controlsys callers that rely on SortSelected (Dare/Care extended pencil, ordered Schur) need a fallback when the reorder is rejected: retry with a perturbed or scaled pencil, use an alternative ordering method, or return a documented error rather than a wrong subspace. The repro is the well-separated 4x4 pencil in gonum ZHGFWA. Files: riccati.go and every Dgges SortSelected call site.

title: CORE: ZPK sortConjugatePairs doubles pair when negative-imag root first; C2D matched wrong
body:

[w14 #44 fuzz/4UAU4O] [CORE] ZPK->TF doubles a conjugate pole/zero pair when the negative-imaginary root is listed first. Repro: NewZPK(nil, []complex128{-1i, 1i}, 1, 0) then transferFunction() gives den [1 0 2 0 1], want [1 0 1]. Poles [-1-2i, -1+2i] give [1 4 14 20 25], want [1 2 5]; (+,-) order is correct. Public symptom: ZPK.StateSpace() returns 4 states and D=0 for a biproper 2-pole ZPK. File zpk.go:322 sortConjugatePairs: it conjugates r to positive imag, then searches k>i for conjR, which is root i itself, finds nothing, appends a pair, and the partner later appends a second pair. Downstream, C2D(matched) breaks whenever a complex root has sin(|Im lambda|*Ts)<0 (an undersampled resonance, omega*Ts>pi, maps the pair to negative-imag-first). Either the value is wrong (corpus testdata/fuzz/FuzzC2DMatched/7aeb2715bda38a0a: Hd(1)=36.40 vs Hc(0)=77.95, 4 states instead of 2) or a correct case becomes an error, 'transfer function is improper' (corpus 16fa0a88fe333983). body:

data.title: CORE: Dare verifyRiccati float64 Hewer noise: accepts 5e-7 X; rejects good X (regression vs base)
data.body:
Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). Common root: double-precision Hewer/Stein step noise in verifyRiccati (newtonTol/newtonStallTol). #17/#19 are value->error regressions vs 1314d32; #16 silent inaccurate X. Cross-ref BFT5QM/QJGONT.

[w15 #16 riccati/review] [Higher priority; BFT5QM blocking criterion] Dare returns an inaccurate X with no error, and the Hewer verification accepts it. This is pre-existing: base 1314d32 and the branch give the same X. Repro: FuzzRiccati input kind=0x93 vals=[940 13 46.5 -2 855 134 0 -600 -20 -25 0.37 0 0.125 -10 -20 3.1] (fuzz id a4a9ec5f51310064, not committed). Problem: n=4, m=2, discrete, unstable eig 2.718 (twice), Q≈1e-12 (C≈1e-6), R=DᵀD+1e-3≈1e6, cond(R)=598, ‖X‖=6e8, no S. The relative Riccati residual is 5.4e-9 (tol 1.9e-9). X error against the 320-bit Hewer oracle is 5.4e-7. A 1-ulp change in A, B, Q or R moves the oracle by 1e-15, and the rounded oracle X has residual 7e-17. verifyRiccati's first double-precision Newton step is 8.6e-9, below newtonTol=1e-8, so the step underestimates the true error by about 60x and the X is accepted. The tightened FuzzRiccati residual gate in f5183fc now catches this family within about 90s of fuzzing; the old Schur widening (4.5e-3) hid it. Files: riccati.go (verifyRiccati/newtonCost, pencilSolution cost scaling).

data.title: CORE: Nyquist on PullDelaysToLFT form fails for |D| 0.77..1 (closure ignores D12*D21)
data.body: Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). [w15 #27 delay/review1] Pre-existing (base and branch): Nyquist on the PullDelaysToLFT form of an ordinary delayed loop with sub-unit feedthrough |D| from about 0.77 to 1 returns an error, while the I/O-delay form of the same loop returns the correct RHPZerosCL. Repro (test helpers from delay_nyquist_test.go): q := quasiLoop{num: []float64{0.9370756617374014, 0.008757399675478617}, den: []float64{1, 1.0258522634845244}, tau: 1.5326090365796423}; q.system(t).Nyquist(nil, 0) gives RHPZerosCL 0 (argument-principle oracle: 0). lft, _ := q.system(t).PullDelaysToLFT(); lft.Nyquist(nil, 0) gives ErrSingularTransform on base 1314d32 and ErrDelayUnsupported ('roots within resolution of the axis at ωτ = 2.38e+08') on fix/delay-wave15. In a 250-case seeded LFT-form sweep, 30 of the cases with |D| > 0.77 fail; every case below 0.77 passes. Fragility: A249 (num [-0.8561202058270045, 0.7368750743551509], den [1, 1.0742800376367483], tau about 0.67025051719364) and A265 flip between OK on arm64 and error on amd64 on a last-bit difference in τ. Likely cause: nyquistEncirclements takes closure = sys.D.At(0,0) and ignores the LFT feedthrough D12·D21. For a single internal delay with D = 0 it then takes the rational-tail loop in continuousHalf toward closure 0, which never settles while |L(j∞)| = |D_lft| ≈ 0.9 oscillates, so it runs on to 1e15 and refine bails out at max depth. Files: nyquist.go (nyquistEncirclements closure, continuousHalf rational tail, refine/markOnContour), delayTailFreq.

data.title: DECISION: descriptor norms JA65GD step 2: singular/improper E semantics; cond(E) limit/equilibrate
data.body:
Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). [w15 #28 norms/JA65GD] JA65GD step 2, singular E in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm (owner decision needed). The MathWorks norm (control/ref/dynamicsystem.norm.html) and hinfnorm (robust/ref/dynamicsystem.hinfnorm.html) pages say nothing about dss, improper or singular-E models, so the precondition for implementing it is not met. Repro: NewDescriptor(A=[-1 1;0.5 -2], B=[1;1], C=[1 0], D=0, E=diag(1,0)) gives H2Norm/HinfNorm -> ErrDescriptorUnsupported wrapping ErrDescriptorSingular. When decided: properExplicitForm / conversionStandardForm (descriptor.go) already reduce proper index-1 models exactly. A continuous improper model plausibly gives Inf for both norms. A discrete improper (non-causal) model has bounded gain on the unit circle, so 'improper means Inf' does not follow there; the owner must settle that case.

[w15 #29 norms/JA65GD] Owner review of the cond(E) limit for norms: normDescriptorCondLimit = 1/sqrt(eps) ≈ 6.7e7 (descriptor.go). A legitimately stiff diagonal E, e.g. diag(1, 1e-9), still returns ErrDescriptorUnsupported. Base also errored, so no regression; loosen it if the owner prefers.

[w15 #30 norms/review0] JA65GD step 2 (planned, not a bug): support singular or improper descriptor E in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm after checking the MathWorks hinfnorm/norm docs. Also consider equilibrating E before the kappa guard, so that badly scaled diagonal E like diag(1e-8,1) is accepted (descriptor.go normExplicitForm).

data.title: CORE: continuous AbsorbDelay turns kept I/O-delay matrix into internal delays (doc/discrete differ)
data.body:
Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). [w15 #34 fuzz/BAY5BF] CORE (minor, semantic): continuous AbsorbDelay(AbsorbInternal, AbsorbInput) still returns internal delays when an I/O-delay matrix is kept. Repro: NewGain([1 2; 3 4], 0); SetInputDelay([0.5, 1]); SetOutputDelay([0.3, 0]); SetDelay([0 0.2; 0.4 0]); AbsorbDelay(AbsorbInternal, AbsorbInput) gives HasInternalDelay() = true, LFT.Tau = [0.2 0.4], Delay = nil. Not covered by delay_absorb_scope_test.go. The test exemption is fzApxKeptIOAsInternal in delay_approx_fuzz_test.go.

[w15 #46 fuzz/review0] [EDGE] Continuous AbsorbDelay(AbsorbInput, AbsorbInternal) on a model with an I/O-delay matrix moves the kept I/O delays into internal delays and leaves them, despite AbsorbInternal. data.title: EDGE: Poly.Equal returns true when NaN in coefficients or tol
data.body:
Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). [w15 #38 fuzz/NWNFLF] [EDGE] Poly.Equal treats NaN differences as equal. Repro: Poly{math.NaN()}.Equal(Poly{5}, 0) == true; Equal(p, q, NaN) is also always true for equal lengths. ## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-21; MathWorks norm/hinfnorm pages checked)
- Equilibration is not a policy question: do pow2 row/column scaling (E→LER, A→LAR, B→LB, C→CR) before the κ(E) test. It is an exact equivalence, so the transfer function is unchanged. Keep the κ(E) error afterwards.
- Singular/improper E: neither page says anything about improper or singular-E models; they only say H∞ = Inf for unstable systems and H2 = Inf when unstable or continuous with nonzero D. Parity is undefined, so keep the documented error for singular E.
- LOW priority: this is feature scope behind the correctness backlog.

Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). Common root: double-precision Hewer/Stein step noise in verifyRiccati (newtonTol/newtonStallTol). #17/#19 are value->error regressions vs 1314d32; #16 silent inaccurate X. Cross-ref BFT5QM/QJGONT.

[w15 #16 riccati/review] [Higher priority; BFT5QM blocking criterion] Dare returns an inaccurate X with no error, and the Hewer verification accepts it. This is pre-existing: base 1314d32 and the branch give the same X. Repro: FuzzRiccati input kind=0x93 vals=[940 13 46.5 -2 855 134 0 -600 -20 -25 0.37 0 0.125 -10 -20 3.1] (fuzz id a4a9ec5f51310064, not committed). Problem: n=4, m=2, discrete, unstable eig 2.718 (twice), Q≈1e-12 (C≈1e-6), R=DᵀD+1e-3≈1e6, cond(R)=598, ‖X‖=6e8, no S. The relative Riccati residual is 5.4e-9 (tol 1.9e-9). X error against the 320-bit Hewer oracle is 5.4e-7. A 1-ulp change in A, B, Q or R moves the oracle by 1e-15, and the rounded oracle X has residual 7e-17. verifyRiccati's first double-precision Newton step is 8.6e-9, below newtonTol=1e-8, so the step underestimates the true error by about 60x and the X is accepted. The tightened FuzzRiccati residual gate in f5183fc now catches this family within about 90s of fuzzing; the old Schur widening (4.5e-3) hid it. Files: riccati.go (verifyRiccati/newtonCost, pencilSolution cost scaling).

[w15 #17 riccati/review] [Value->error regression on fix/riccati-wave15] Dare returns ErrNoStabilizing where base 1314d32 returned a near-accurate X. Repro: FuzzRiccati input kind=0x75 vals=[397 13 46.5 -2 855 268 0 -600 -20 27 0.37 -64 0.0625 -10 -10 3.1] (fuzz id 23ae51b4794d4168). Problem: n=3, m=3, discrete, Q≈1e-12, R≈1e5..8e5 with cond 1.44e9, no S. On base, X agrees with the 320-bit Hewer oracle to 9.4e-8. A 1-ulp change in B or R moves X by 2.7e-8, so base was within about 3.5x of the precision limit. Base rcnd is 7.9e-4 and the fuzz target counted the case as an ill-conditioned skip. Diagnosis: verifyRiccati's double-precision Hewer steps are noise-dominated, wandering 1e-5..1e-3 for all 12 steps. The best step, 1.9e-5, is above newtonStallTol=1e-6, so the solve is rejected. Files: riccati.go verifyRiccati (newtonStallTol/stall exit).

[w15 #19 riccati/review] Fast-sampled Dare with S=C'D and ill-conditioned R: branch tip f5183fc (and 2016b33) returns ErrNoStabilizing where base 1314d32 is accurate (rel err 3e-8..9e-7). This was already on the tip; my change did not cause it. Repro, seed-1 sweep case 757: n=5, m=3, A = expm(Ac*dt) with A within 1.3e-4 of I. R=[4812.562556102683 -5744.385549251563 -8964.467126542602; -5744.385549251563 6856.630955448088 10700.194516334564; -8964.467126542602 10700.194516334564 16698.311977111804]. S (5x3, row-major)=[-46.33924068437183 55.31158540298616 86.3171325828967; -66.2950935508293 79.13135119566881 123.48934283578767; -5.823723950719496 6.951331094475053 10.847979918453428; 131.7904357144906 -157.30810070820263 -245.48897100426493; 133.12202608916857 -158.89751766115745 -247.9693539630636]. A, B and Q were dumped but are not reproduced here; regenerate them from the same seeded sweep. Dare returns ErrNoStabilizing in both modes; base gives 4.75e-8 (default) / 3.05e-6 (NoScaling). Every pass of verifyRiccati stalls with Hewer steps of 4e-6..1.3e-4, which is noise from the near-I Stein solve; R-whitening does not help. Other cases: seed-1 43, 814, 1366 and seed-2 952. Files: riccati.go (verifyRiccati, newtonCost, dlyap).

## Note (coordinator, 2026-10-21)
#17 and #19 are value→error flips in merged wave 15 (PR pending): base returned X at 9.4e-8 and 4.75e-8..3e-6 relative error, and the branch returns ErrNoStabilizing. They were accepted because base was outside the 1e-9 accuracy bar and cond(R) is up to 1.4e9.
The fix must make verifyRiccati's Hewer/Newton verification noise-aware: scale tolerances by eps·(‖A‖²‖X‖+‖Q‖+‖BᵀXB‖) rather than absolute newtonTol/newtonStallTol, and recover these cases without accepting #16. Priority CORE for wave 16.
